knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=3 x z + y$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,- v,\,- v^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.

*Hint: You can use the fact that $‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1}.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

Notice that we are told that the norm of the fundamental vector product for our surface is

$$
‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖=\sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1}.
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3 x z + y)\,{|}_{x=u\,y=- v\,z=- v^{2}} \\  & =3\cdot (u)\cdot (-v^{2})+(-v) \\  & =- 3 u v^{2} - v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{4 v^{2} + 1} \left(- 3 u v^{2} - v\right)\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Constructing Surface Integrals Over Parametric Surfaces

question.:question/problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=3 x - 2 y^{2} z$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨2 u v,\,- u,\,3 u - v^{2}⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(2 u v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(- u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(3 u - v^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2 v,\,-1,\,3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(2 u v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(- u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(3 u - v^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2 u,\,0,\,- 2 v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 2 v & -1 & 3 \\ 2 u & 0 & - 2 v\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 3 \\ 0 & - 2 v\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}2 v & 3 \\ 2 u & - 2 v\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}2 v & -1 \\ 2 u & 0\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨2 v,\,6 u + 4 v^{2},\,2 u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨2 v,\,6 u + 4 v^{2},\,2 u⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(2 v)^{2}+(6 u + 4 v^{2})^{2}+(2 u)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{40 u^{2} + 48 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3 x - 2 y^{2} z)\,{|}_{x=2 u v\,y=- u\,z=3 u - v^{2}} \\  & =6 u v-2\cdot (- u)^{2}\cdot (3 u - v^{2}) \\  & =- 6 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\left(- 6 u^{3} + 2 u^{2} v^{2} + 6 u v\right) \sqrt{40 u^{2} + 48 u v^{2} + 16 v^{4} + 4 v^{2}}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A
$$

Consider the surface integral of the function 
$f(x,y,z)=3 x^{2} + y^{2}$ 
over the parametric surface 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u,\,v⟩
$$

for $(u,v)\in D⊆{R}^{2}.$ What is the missing expression? Choose an integrand equal to the required expression as a function on $D$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface integral of a scalar function $f$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+0} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(u,v)) & =(3 x^{2} + y^{2})\,{|}_{x=u\,y=u\,z=v} \\  & =3\cdot (u)^{2}+u^{2} \\  & =4 u^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}f(r(u,v))‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\,\sqrt{2} \cdot 4 u^{2}\,\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
